source.title: Half-awake to the risk of predation.

confidence_rationale: Landmark Nature paper with a clean quantitative behavioural manipulation (group edge vs centre) and directional eye-orientation data. The graded, facultative control of sleep depth under risk is exactly the shape question the synthesis needed answered.
failure_signatures: If REE implements a safety term as an all-or-nothing permit and shows a bimodal sleep distribution (full cycles or none) across a hazard gradient, Rattenborg predicts this is wrong-shaped: the biological response is monotone-graded in risk. Diagnostic: sleep duration/depth as a function of threat magnitude should be continuous and monotone, not a step.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Mallards at the edge of a group increased unihemispheric slow-wave sleep from 12.4% to 31.8% relative to birds at the centre, and during unihemispheric sleep directed the open eye away from the group centre 86.2% of the time. Birds can detect approaching predators during unihemispheric sleep and increase its use as predation risk rises. Sleep and wakefulness are controlled simultaneously in different brain regions.
mapping.ree_translation: The decisive source for the synthesis's recommendation that a safety term be GRADED rather than boolean. The risk response here is not permit/refuse: it is a continuous reallocation of how much of the system sleeps, plus directional steering of the retained vigilance. This is the point at which the local-sleep thread (Krueger, Vyazovskiy) and the safety thread meet -- partial sleep under threat is mechanically natural only if sleep need and sleep state are regionally decomposable. REE cannot do this today (whole-agent sleep), so the duration/depth factor is the available approximation and should be named as an approximation.
mapping.mapping_caveat: REE has no hemispheric or regional decomposition of its sleep state and no sensory vigilance channel that could stay open during a sleep cycle, so the mechanism cannot be implemented in V3. The transferable content is the SHAPE of the risk response (graded, partial, retained-watch), not the mechanism. The 12.4%/31.8% figures are mallard-specific and are not parameter anchors for REE.
mapping.source_context: Behavioural and EEG study of mallards in a four-bird row, edge vs centre positions.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality very high with clean quantitative contrast. Transfer risk elevated because the mechanism (unihemispheric sleep) has no V3 analogue; only the response shape transfers.
